title: Child Custody in Bangladesh When One Parent Lives Abroad: Guardianship, Visitation and Travel
metaTitle: Child Custody in Bangladesh When One Parent Lives Abroad
metaDescription: How Bangladeshi courts decide child custody and guardianship when a parent lives abroad: Family Court procedure, welfare of the child, visitation, relocation and cross-border issues.
heroIntro: A parent works in the Gulf, UK or North America, the other parent lives with the child in Bangladesh, and the marriage breaks down. Who gets custody, who can take the child abroad, and what happens if one parent refuses to return the child? This guide is written by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court of Bangladesh, for Bangladeshis living in the UK, USA, UAE, Canada and elsewhere. For case-specific help call or WhatsApp the chamber on 01712655546.

quickAnswer.heading: Custody Basics
points: Custody and guardianship cases are decided by the Family Court under the Family Courts Ordinance 1985 and the Guardians and Wards Act 1890.
The welfare of the child is the controlling test; religion-based custody rules are applied in light of it.
Mothers commonly keep young children; fathers remain natural guardians and must pay maintenance.
A parent living abroad can file or defend a case through an advocate and Power of Attorney, and may give evidence by video.
Taking a child abroad without the other parent's consent or a court order can lead to litigation and criminal complaints.

sections.content:
Custody (hizanat) means physical care of the child. Guardianship means legal authority over the child's person and property. Under Muslim law, the father is the natural guardian, but the mother usually has custody of young children: boys generally until about seven years and girls until puberty, although courts treat these ages as guidelines, not rigid limits. The welfare of the child can override them.

This article is general legal information, not legal advice. Fees, forms and procedures change; confirm current requirements with the relevant office or a qualified advocate before acting.

The Family Court in the district where the child ordinarily lives has jurisdiction. Applications are made under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890, read with the Family Courts Ordinance 1985. The court first tries mediation and reconciliation, then hears evidence from both sides and may order a social inquiry or interview the child.

• The child's age, health and emotional bond with each parent.
  • Stability of home, education and schooling.
  • Each parent's income, conduct and ability to provide care.
  • Wishes of an older child.
  • Whether a parent is in a position to maintain regular contact if the child is moved.

A parent abroad can:

  • File or defend the case through an advocate with a notarised and attested Power of Attorney (see PoA guide).
  • Give evidence by video if the court permits.
  • Apply for interim visitation or video call access.
  • Seek an order for maintenance of the child.

If the parent abroad wants custody, the court will ask how the child's schooling, residence and contact with the other parent will be arranged. A realistic plan matters.

Courts can order structured visitation: weekend contact, holiday stays, or video calls. If one parent wants to relocate the child abroad, the court's permission is usually needed when there is a dispute. A parent who removes a child abroad without consent risks a custody order against him or her, and possible criminal action. Bangladesh is not a party to the Hague Convention on child abduction, which makes cross-border enforcement harder, so negotiate and document arrangements early.

1. Gather the child's birth certificate, school records and proof of residence.
  2. Keep a record of financial support and communication.
  3. Seek interim orders for custody, visitation and maintenance at the start.
  4. Consider mediation or a written parenting agreement approved by the court.
  5. Obtain a mirror order or recognition abroad if the child will live there.

faqs.question: Who gets custody of a child in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: The Family Court decides on the child's welfare; mothers commonly keep young children, but this is not an absolute rule.

faqs.question: Can the father take the child abroad without the mother's consent?
faqs.answer: If there is a dispute, doing so can lead to court orders and legal action. Get the court's permission or the other parent's written consent.

faqs.question: Can I fight a custody case from abroad?
faqs.answer: Yes, through an advocate and Power of Attorney, and by giving evidence by video if allowed.

faqs.question: Does a foreign custody order apply in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: It is not automatically enforced. A Bangladesh court considers the child's welfare, so you may need to apply there as well.

faqs.question: Is child maintenance compulsory?
faqs.answer: Yes. The father has a duty to maintain his children, and the court can order it.
